subject: Career
title: Market Rate: Finding Your Number
description: A short lesson to help you apply Market Rate: Finding Your Number.

hook.text: You can't negotiate if you don't know what the job is worth. Research comes before everything.

buildup.text: Glassdoor, Levels.fyi, Payscale, and LinkedIn Salary give real compensation data by role and city.

discovery.text: Look at the range, not just the median. Your experience and skills place you somewhere in that band.

twist.text: Company size matters hugely. The same title at a startup vs. a bank can differ by 40%.

climax.text: Collect three to five data points. Overlapping ranges give you a defensible target.

punchline.text: Know the market before you name a number.

quiz.question: Why should you research salary ranges before negotiating?
options: To set a defensible target based on market data

details.summary: Finding your market rate requires cross-referencing multiple data sources including Glassdoor, Levels.fyi, Payscale, Bureau of Labor Statistics data, and peer conversations. The intersection of role, location, experience, and industry defines a realistic salary band you can defend.
details.whyItMatters: Negotiating without market data is like bidding at an auction blindfolded. Precise benchmarks transform a request into a justified business case.
takeaways: Use at least three independent sources for salary benchmarks
Adjust for geography, company stage, and total compensation
Peer conversations often reveal the most accurate market data

faq.question: Which salary research tool is the most reliable overall?
faq.answer: No single tool is definitive. Glassdoor provides broad coverage, Levels.fyi excels for tech roles, and the Bureau of Labor Statistics offers government-validated medians. Triangulating across at least three sources produces the most accurate picture.

faq.question: How do I adjust salary data for cost-of-living differences?
faq.answer: Use cost-of-living indices from sources like the Council for Community and Economic Research. Multiply the target city's index against the data city's index. Remote roles may also use geographic pay bands published by larger companies.
